meta.subtitle: Profitable and generating cash, at under 5x forward earnings, but credit risk, funding costs and founder control justify caution

analystCommentary:
Pagaya turned profitable in FY25, with net income attributable to shareholders of $81.4 million against a loss of $(401.4) million in FY24. Network Volume kept growing in the second quarter of 2026, and the operating margin reached 28.9%.

At $18.01 on October 2, 2026 the shares sit between the 52-week low of $10.40 and the high of $32.04. All 11 covering analysts rate Buy, and the shares trade at 4.9x NTM earnings.

We are less positive than the Street. Pagaya's revenue depends on investors continuing to fund the loans its Partners originate, and the MD&A says its cost of capital has risen. The company also holds risk retention positions that expose it directly to credit losses. A low multiple is common for businesses with that exposure.

We rate PGY HOLD with an $18–$26 target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Pagaya Technologies Ltd. is a technology company that uses data science and AI to help financial institutions approve more loan applications. Its Partners, ranging from financial technology companies to incumbent banks, auto finance providers and residential real estate service providers, send applications they would otherwise decline to Pagaya's network. Loans originated with Pagaya's help are bought by Financing Vehicles, including Pagaya-sponsored asset-backed securitizations and forward flow arrangements with third-party investors.

Pagaya earns network AI fees, contract fees, interest income and investment income. Its main products include Decline Monetization, Dual Look and First Look, along with customer acquisition tools.

The company was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in New York, New York. It is incorporated in Israel and governed by the Israel Companies Law.

thesis.body: Pagaya has shown it can grow and be profitable, and the forward multiple is low. But its earnings depend on credit markets: investor appetite for consumer loans, the cost of funding and the performance of the loans it helps originate. Our probability-weighted fair value implies upside, but the downside in a credit downturn is large enough that the reward/risk falls short of a BUY (see Valuation).

catalysts: Further diversification of the investor funding base.
Stable credit performance in Pagaya-sponsored securitizations.
Easing of the funding-cost pressure the MD&A describes.
risks: A rise in consumer credit losses.
Higher funding costs or weaker investor demand.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $1.3B, up {+25.6%+}, after growth of 30.0% in FY24. Operating margin improved from -3.2% in FY23 and 6.7% in FY24 to 20.9% in FY25, and diluted EPS turned positive at $0.93 from -$5.66. The 10-K credits the improvement in Adjusted EBITDA, to $371.0 million from $210.4 million, to FRLPC improvement initiatives and disciplined cost management.

In the second quarter of 2026 revenue was $365.6M, up 15.1%, and operating margin was 28.9%. Network Volume, the main revenue driver, rose to $3,535 million from $2,648 million.

The counter-case: revenue growth is slowing, from the FY25 rate to the latest quarter's, and the trailing net margin is 9.6%, well below the operating margin. The 10-K itself warns that growth rates have slowed and may continue to slow.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Our data does not report total debt or a current ratio for FY25, so we cannot assess leverage from the summary figures. The key balance-sheet exposure is the risk retention holdings: the 10-K says these increased during 2025 as a result of ABS issuances, and that the magnitude of potential losses has increased with them.

Those holdings mean Pagaya is not a pure fee business. If the loans in its securitizations perform poorly, it bears part of the loss directly.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $224.7M in FY25, a 17.8% FCF margin, after negative or thin margins in FY22 to FY24. The trailing FCF yield is 16.8%. Capital expenditure is small.

The swing to strong cash generation is the most important change in the business. Its durability depends on funding markets staying open, so we would want to see it sustained through a period of credit stress before relying on it.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $18.01 PGY trades at 12.9x trailing earnings, 4.9x NTM earnings, ~4.4x FY27E earnings and 1.1x trailing sales.

Consensus EPS of $3.70 for FY26E and $4.13 for FY27E is far above FY25 diluted EPS of $0.93. The consensus basis is not stated; the company reports Adjusted EBITDA and other non-GAAP measures, so the estimates may be on an adjusted basis.

The Street is uniformly positive: 11 Buy ratings, with a consensus target of $28.91, a median of $27.00 and a range of $23.00–$36.00.

We have no peer multiples to compare against. In our view, the low multiple reflects the market's view of credit and funding risk, not only of growth.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Network Volume keeps growing, credit performance stays stable and funding costs ease. The market re-rates Pagaya as a durable earner, taking the shares into the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Pagaya delivers close to consensus, funding remains available at today's costs, and the multiple recovers modestly. The shares settle below the low end of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Consumer credit deteriorates, losses rise on risk retention holdings and investors pull back from funding. Network Volume and earnings fall, and the shares return toward the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it assumes only that today's conditions persist. Bear carries more weight than Bull because the MD&A already reports a higher cost of capital and the 10-K reports larger risk retention exposure. Bull needs easier funding as well as continued growth.

The result is a weighted fair value of $20.70, an expected upside of +14.9% and a bear-case downside of -38.9%. The expected upside is meaningful, but the bear-case downside is too large relative to it for a BUY.

Our $18–$26 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Pagaya reports a single segment. Management describes two sides of the business: a fee-generating product suite and a capital efficiency side that funds the assets. The main operating measure is Network Volume, which was $6,159 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026 against $5,048 million a year earlier.

moatFactors.name: Data network
moatFactors.body: Pagaya says it has evaluated more than $4.2 trillion in application volume since inception, and that more data leads to more efficient pricing. That data asset is difficult for a new entrant to replicate quickly.

moatFactors.name: Partner integration
moatFactors.body: Once integrated, Partners tend to scale origination volume on the network, and the MD&A says Pagaya's share of their originations tends to increase over time. The counter-case is that Partners can add other providers.

moatFactors.name: Funding network
moatFactors.body: Pagaya has diversified its investor base: its top 5 investors accounted for approximately 44% of total funding in the six months ended June 30, 2026, against 52% a year earlier. Funding remains its point of dependence, since its revenue relies on investor appetite.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The data network and Partner integrations give Pagaya an advantage in underwriting declined applications. Its dependence on outside investors to fund the loans means the business is only as durable as its access to capital, which the 10-K lists among its key risks.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$1.5B, up 16%, and FY27E revenue of $1.7B.
Network Volume growth in the second quarter outpaced revenue growth, which suggests continued demand from Partners.
Pagaya continues to introduce new asset types, products and services, which the MD&A says lets Partners expand their relationship.
The MD&A says the cost of capital has risen and that conversion ratios have been adjusted to meet investor return expectations, which may constrain the pace of growth.

management.leadership: Gal Krubiner is Chief Executive Officer, and the Board is led by an independent Chairman, Avi Zeevi, per the proxy statement dated July 2026. Co-founders Yahav Yulzari and Avital Pardo also serve on the Board and are employed by the company. The team has delivered the shift to profitability and positive cash flow shown in Financials.
management.capitalAllocation: Pagaya pays no dividend, and our data shows no repurchase amounts for FY21 to FY25. Its main capital decision is how much risk retention it holds in its securitizations, which supports funding but exposes the balance sheet to credit losses. In our view, holders should watch whether risk retention keeps rising relative to the business.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated July 2026, the Board determined that Avi Zeevi, Alison Davis, Jason Gardner, Harvey Golub, Asheet Mehta and Dan Petrozzo are independent director nominees, while Mr. Krubiner, Mr. Pardo, Mr. Yulzari and Ms. Rosen are not because they are employed by the company. The Board held six meetings during fiscal year 2025. As an Israeli company, Pagaya applies the Israel Companies Law to related-person transactions, with its Audit and Finance Committee reviewing extraordinary transactions. The independent Chairman is a positive; the founders' voting control (see Insider ownership) limits what independent directors can do.
management.insiderOwnership:
Pagaya has a dual-class structure. As of June 15, 2026 Gal Krubiner held 43.3% of total voting power, Avital Pardo 42.5% and Yahav Yulzari 40.1%, mostly through Class B Ordinary Shares, and all directors and executive officers as a group held 81.8%. Oak HC/FT Partners II, L.P. held 5.7% of the Class A Ordinary Shares.

For public holders, this means the founders control shareholder votes. Their economic alignment is strong, but outside shareholders have little say over strategy or governance.

idiosyncratic: Credit performance: the 10-K warns that poor performance of the Financing Vehicles would likely reduce revenue, net income and cash flow, and impair Pagaya's ability to raise capital.
Risk retention: the larger risk retention holdings described in Financials increase Pagaya's direct exposure to loan losses.
Funding: the MD&A says the conflict between Israel, the U.S. and Iran that erupted in February 2026 has increased Pagaya's cost of capital and may diminish investor appetite for risk assets.
Control: the founders' voting power, set out in Management, limits the influence of public shareholders.
risks.systemic: The MD&A says elevated interest rates and inflation increase borrowing costs and could lead to higher delinquencies, defaults and charge-offs, reducing investor returns and demand for assets from the platform. Regional bank stress or broader liquidity problems could disrupt funding flows. Pagaya's earnings are therefore closely tied to the consumer credit cycle.

body: HOLD, target range $18–$26, based on the scenarios in Valuation.

We would move to BUY on evidence that funding costs are easing and credit performance is holding through a period of stress, or on a lower share price. We would turn more cautious if delinquencies rise or if investors pull back from Pagaya's securitizations.
